theme.name: Tourism's economic importance and record growth
theme.claim: Tourism is a vital and growing UK industry, providing 1.6 million jobs, record overseas and domestic spend and over £62bn GVA, so its success is worth sustaining and spreading.

text.line: The industry provides 1.6 million jobs across the country.
In 2015, we saw the greatest number of overseas visits to the UK on record, bringing £22.1 billion into our economy.
Domestic overnight spend also hit a record high of £19.6 billion in England.
Tourism is one of the UK’s most important industries with it directly responsible for 1.6 million jobs at all entry levels throughout the UK. ** (Reference: 1)
Last year was record-breaking, with tourism generating over £62bn in GVA to the UK economy.
Domestic overnight spend reached a new high of £19.6bn in England, and the UK attracted more overseas visits than ever before, generating over £22bn of export earnings. ** (Reference: 2)

theme.name: Spending concentrated in London
theme.claim: Over 50% of international visitor spend remains in London because many overseas visitors never venture beyond the capital, even though some regions are growing faster than London, so the sector needs rebalancing.

text.line: But many overseas visitors never venture beyond London, so over 50% of their spending is in the capital.
The South East, South West, West Midlands and North East have all seen international visitor rates and spend grow faster than London over the past year.

Further, the rate of growth in visits and spend to many regions was faster than in London - as visitors flocked to see our world class heritage sites, stunning countryside, and to capture moments from Glastonbury to the Rugby World Cup.
However, with over 50% of international visitor spend still in the capital, there is more to be done to rebalance the sector, boosting jobs and growth right across the country.

theme.name: Barriers to exploring beyond London
theme.claim: Visitors are deterred from exploring regions by fear of driving on the left and by difficulty finding information and booking tickets for public transport, and by the reliance on air gateways and London as the first-time destination, so transport and connectivity must improve.

text.line: Britain’s road system is an excellent means of exploring the country.

However, many international visitors are fearful of driving on the ‘wrong’ side of the road, so it’s vital that they feel confident navigating our system of public transport, if they are to explore beyond London.
However, international visitors can find it difficult to find the information they need, in the right language, to book the right tickets at the right price, and to be assured of a seamless journey.
In 2015, 73% of international visits to the UK were made by air.

However, the roll-out of smart ticketing infrastructure, the development of route-planning apps like Rome2Rio and reduced international roaming charges are key to giving international visitors the confidence to use these services.

theme.name: Fragmented industry and structural constraints
theme.claim: The diverse, fragmented and competitive sector finds collaboration costly despite its collective benefit, and is mainly small and seasonal businesses, which makes co-ordinated promotion and growth hard without government action.

text.line: The overall success of the tourism industry is contingent on its ability to work together to promote what it has to offer.
However, the costs of collaboration are high, as the sector is diverse, fragmented and competitive, and this can deter action - despite it being collectively beneficial.
The tourism sector is overwhelmingly comprised of SMEs providing employment in some of our most rural communities and enjoyment to millions.
Multiple Government Departments, from Transport to Home Office to DCLG, and DEFRA, invest in the success of Britain’s tourism industry.
Tourism is a devolved matter, but a number of policy levers—from aviation connectivity to aspects of the regulatory framework and immigration—are reserved.
But there is still work to be done in promoting the whole of the UK.
